generatedProse.concept-context: For a psychology student, this is one habit across every research placement, lab practical and voluntary role. Before a placement in a clinic or lab you set aims, perhaps to learn an assessment tool or see how a team runs a study. While there you act and seek feedback; afterwards you evidence what you learned for your portfolio. Each placement then sharpens how you aim at the next.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students complete a run of placements: a research lab, then an assistant role in a mental health service. One arrives each time with no aims and writes up only what they observed. The other sets aims, volunteers to help run a study, asks for feedback, and records what each role taught about working with people and data. By the second placement, that student is trusted with more and can evidence clear, specific learning.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, making the most of placements is one continuing practice, not a box ticked once. You aim, act and evidence on each research or clinical experience, and let each one shape how you approach the next. Over your degree, that habit builds both your skills and the evidence a future employer or course will want to see.

check.body: A student sets aims for a placement, takes initiative and seeks feedback throughout, then evidences what they learned. They carry one lesson into their next placement, which goes better. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That making the most of experience works as one continuing practice, run across placement after placement.
_items.feedback: Yes. The whole loop ran, and carrying it forward improved the next placement.

_items.text: That the first placement was a better opportunity than most.
_items.feedback: The point is not the placement itself. It is the practice the student ran on it.

_items.text: That evidencing learning is the only part that matters.
_items.feedback: Evidencing is one part. Aiming and acting came first and made the evidence possible.

_items.text: That this only works for students who are naturally confident.
_items.feedback: The practice helped this student whatever their starting point. It is the habit, not the personality.
